subject: Re: MAP & option decision — deployment mode and region preferences
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brightlinetx.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@brightlinetx.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0500
Subject: MAP kickoff + deployment constraints

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked promising. We want to pull together a short MAP so our internal committee can sign off on a PoC and procurement. Two hard constraints from Legal/IT: patient data must remain in EU region and we need to validate encryption-at-rest key control (KMS/HSM) before any production go-live.

High-level asks from our side:
- A MAP with milestones for evaluation (POC -> security review -> procurement) and estimated dates
- Clear recommendation for deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private) given PHI residency and latency targets (~<120ms 95th pct to our EU region)
- List of compliance artifacts you can provide (SOC 2, pen test summary, data flow diagram)

Can you send a draft MAP and note whether a Hosted EU offering will meet the residency + KMS needs or if Dedicated/Private is required? We want to close the procurement decision by 2026-12-15.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Head of Platform Integrations
Brightline Therapeutics

[Attachment: initial_requirements.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)]

From: Priyom Das <priom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brightlinetx.com>
Cc: Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@brightlinetx.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + deployment constraints

Hi Sarah — appreciate the clear constraints and timeline. I attached a draft MAP (Brightline_MAP_v1.xlsx) that lays out the milestones and owners. Short answers up front:

- Residency: We can host within eu-west-1 for the Hosted product and ensure data residency for request/response logs. For stronger custody (customer-controlled keys, HSM-backed KMS and private networking), Dedicated or Private will be necessary.
- Recommendation: Start POC on Hosted (eu) for functional validation and speed to value, then evaluate Dedicated for production if you need HSM-backed keys or stricter network isolation. Private (on-prem) is available if procurement/legal require full air-gapped control — longer lead time.

Key dates in the draft MAP:
- POC kickoff: 2026-11-22
- Security evidence review (SOC 2, KMS design): 2026-11-29
- Procurement readiness decision (Hosted vs Dedicated): 2026-12-08
- Contract signature target: 2026-12-15

Attachments included: Brightline_MAP_v1.xlsx, SOC2_high_level.pdf, network_peering_diagram.png.

Next steps: can your IT team review the network diagram and KMS notes by 11/24? If you confirm the EU residency and are OK with a Hosted POC, we can provision a dedicated EU-hosted instance for you to test within 48 hours.

Best,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: SOC2_high_level.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brightlinetx.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + deployment constraints

Hi all — quick technical context from infra:

- Latency: our EU-hosted nodes (eu-west-1) typically show 80–110ms 95th to EU app frontends; Dedicated in the same region reduces variability and can push the 95th down to ~60–80ms depending on instance sizing and batching.
- KMS/HSM: Hosted supports BYOK via customer-managed KMS in the region (bring your own key, rotated via your KMS). For HSM-backed KMS where Redwood does not have custodial access, Dedicated or Private is required — we can integrate with your cloud HSM if provided.
- Networking: We can support VPC peering and PrivateLink for Dedicated and offer secure egress paths for Hosted. Private deployments can be fully air-gapped if you need that level.

If Brightline is primarily worried about PHI residency but wants fastest time-to-eval, Hosted (eu) + BYOK is the practical path. If Legal requires an HSM model where Brightline owns the only root key, plan for Dedicated.

Happy to jump on a quick call with your infra folks.

—Karthik

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@brightlinetx.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marco Diaz <marco.diaz@brightlinetx.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Nov 2026 08:39:00 -0000
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + deployment constraints

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifications from our IT/security team after reviewing the diagram and SOC2 notes:

- BYOK in Hosted is acceptable for the PoC only if keys never leave our tenant and we control rotation. Can you confirm that Redwood will not retain a copy of the customer key material in Hosted mode?
- For Dedicated, procurement will need a pricing delta and lead time. Can you provide a ballpark monthly cost for a Dedicated EU pool supporting 100 TPS and the expected provisioning lead time?
- Legal wants to see the pen test executive summary and any subcontractor lists (where logs or telemetry might transit the US).

We can review the MAP spreadsheet during a call next week. Our internal deadline to pick a path for procurement is 2026-12-08.

Regards,
Sarah

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + deployment constraints — updated MAP and pricing punchlist

Hi Sarah — following up with the items Legal/IT requested and a clearer close plan: 

1) Keys: Hosted (eu) supports BYOK via your cloud KMS; Redwood will never store raw key material. We will use KMS APIs for encryption/decryption and support key rotation policies you configure. I attached a short tech note and the network diagram updated with telemetry flows.

2) Pen test summary & subcontractors: SOC2_high_level.pdf includes the high level; I can share the pen test executive summary under NDA — will request from Security. Subcontractor list: we use a managed CDN and cloud provider in eu-west-1; logs that Redwood processes for observability are stored in-region unless you ask for cross-region export.

3) Pricing: rough Dedicated EU pool estimate for 100 TPS (with reserved capacity and 99.9% SLO): ~$55K/month. Provisioning lead time: 4–6 weeks for capacity scheduling and compliance checks.

Updated MAP milestones (attached Brightline_MAP_v1.xlsx, sheet 'v1.1'):
- POC kickoff (Hosted, eu): 2026-11-22 — complete
- Security evidence delivery: 2026-11-29 — in progress
- Legal & procurement decision (Hosted vs Dedicated): 2026-12-08
- Contract signature target: 2026-12-15

If procurement requires HSM-only key custody, we should plan to move to Dedicated for production and reserve capacity now to avoid calendar delays.

Can we set a 30-minute sync Thursday 2026-12-01 to walk procurement/legal through the difference and close the decision? Monica — can you coordinate the call?

Thanks,
Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Priyom / team — thanks for the speedy follow-up and the pricing transparency. We reviewed the updated MAP and legal confirmed: if we can get the pen test executive summary under NDA and a written statement that Hosted (eu) will not retain raw key material, Legal is willing to approve a Hosted POC with BYOK. Procurement still needs the Dedicated estimate as a fallback.

Confirming the 12/01 30-minute sync — 10:00 AM CET / 04:00 AM EST won't work for our team; can we do 11:00 AM CET / 05:00 AM EST instead? Also please include a line item in the MAP for acceptance criteria (latency 95th < 120ms, functional test set pass rate >= 95%).

If we can get the pen test exec summary by 11/30 and the key custody statement in writing, Brightline will move forward with the Hosted POC and aim to make a procurement call by 12/08.

Best,
Sarah Liu
Head of Platform Integrations
Brightline Therapeutics
